textPlacement.assessment: Both contexts keep pouring to a manageable jug and a little water, with adult help and partial repetition, while the chart and appendix ages remain distinct.
Fetching one shoe and receiving more help remain enough in both ages, making the reachable home for shoes a shared convenience rather than a demand for independent dressing.
Steady walking, cut flower stems and supervision remain visible, and partial plant care does not obligate a family to complete arrangements or maintain a garden.
Carrying one garment remains a sufficient contribution, with sorting and supervised hanging presented as distinct optional parts rather than added duties.
The contexts keep tools and movement manageable, while the invitation permits shared cleanup, imperfect results and stopping before overwhelm.
The older placement preserves brief voluntary participation, hands-on assistance and the separate later knife example without treating the browse age as permission for every tool.
A small real contribution remains an invitation, with help and the child’s continuing need for movement and connection retained throughout an outing.
The earlier plate-return example and fuller later table work remain distinct, with one manageable contribution and adult help sufficient at either age.
